content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"This judge text evaluates a Matthew 1:16 link where the parties' chain answers are in view, and it resolves the link by the isolated ambiguity of the verse's wording.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"never verse by verse: read as forbidding an UNDERDETERMINED call on Matthew 1:16 based on its isolated ambiguity, versus allowing such a call only after weighing the chains by footing.","why":"The judge treats the single verse's ambiguity as enough to leave the link underdetermined instead of weighing the parties' chains by footing as K-C requires."}
